content.text: LÃ³rum is a classic Hungarian compendium game played with a 32-card German-suited pack. It consists of a series of diverse 'contracts' or mini-games, traditionally eight in total. Each player takes a turn as the 'declarer' who chooses the round. It is a game of variety, where players must switch from trick-avoidance (negative) to shedding (positive) strategies within a single session. It is deeply rooted in Central European cafe culture.
Developed from the 19th-century 'Quodlibet' and 'King' families of games, tailored for the 32-card Hungarian Tell deck.
32 cards (Hearts, Bells, Leaves, Acorns). Ace is high.
Each player receives 8 cards. The dealer rotation ensures everyone gets to lead each contract type once.
